title: Find the First 5-7-5 Haiku
prompt:
Implement `find_first_haiku(sentence, syllables) -> list[list[str]] | None`. Extract words from `sentence` with the pattern `[A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)?`, lowercase them, and look up every normalized word in `syllables`. Each count must be a positive integer.

Return the earliest contiguous sequence of words that can be split into three consecutive lines with syllable totals 5, then 7, then 5. Return the three normalized word lists, or `None` when no such sequence exists. Earliest means the smallest starting word index. Raise `ValueError` if an extracted word has no syllable entry or an entry is not a positive integer.

This is a practice reconstruction of the Faire prompt's unspecified punctuation and unknown-word behavior, while preserving its prefix-sum search task.

example.input: find_first_haiku('A a a a a b b b b b b b c c c c c', {'a': 1, 'b': 1, 'c': 1})
example.reasoning: The whole sentence is the first contiguous 5-7-5 sequence.
